topics: Final latency & memory benchmarks on dedicated cluster
questions: Do we have a clear SLO for p50/p95/p99 under expected load?
Can the current KV cache warmup approach meet the cold-start latency target?
Is the KMS test coverage sufficient for SOC2 audit?
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Evan, Maya, Jordan, Priya, Samir

[00:00] Evan: Ok hey everyone, thanks for joining, um let's do a quick check-in on launch readiness, we've got about an hour. I shared the deck and the benchmark sheet in the chat, link: drive/launch-readiness-deck and drive/benchmarks (see note).

[00:33] Maya: Yep saw the deck, thanks Evan. Main things I want to confirm are autoscale thresholds and the canary windows, also any recent perf regressions?

[01:05] Jordan: I ran a quick pass last night, preliminary numbers look fine but I did see a spike on p99 when sequence length hit 2k for a subset. Could be KV cash warm-up, sorry K V cash, that prefix cache isn't fully warmed in the test. I'll re-run with longer warm-up.

[01:40] Priya: Are we testing with the dedicated cluster config? We should make sure the kernel selection matches prod GPUs. I saw some mismatch on the kernel selection in the emu run which drove up latency a bit.

[02:10] Samir: For the dedicated nodes I used the same compile flags as the earlier rollout, but there might be a mismatch in the compilation profile, I'll verify. Also we need to have the drain/scale policy codified in the playbook.

[02:45] Evan: Good. Jordan, can you do a full bench on the dedicated cluster with a longer KV cache warmup and both 1k and 2k sequences and share the sheet by Sunday?

[03:10] Jordan: Yep I can do that, plan is to run ycsb-like load with varying arrival rates. I'll include token breakdown and cost per 1k tokens.

[04:00] Maya: On autoscaling, proposal is: scale-up at 70% sustained utilization, scale-down after 10m below 50%, with a canary of 5% traffic for 30 minutes. Thoughts?

[04:37] Priya: 30 minutes might be short for catching intermittent OOMs or mem leaks, I'd like 60 minutes for canary at least for bigger models. Could we do 30m for smaller models and 60m for the 2B+ ones?

[05:12] Evan: That sounds reasonable. Let's do model-size-based canary windows: 30m for <2B, 60m for >=2B. Maya, update the playbook.

[05:40] Samir: Also, rollback plan: immediate traffic re-route to hosted region or previous model snapshot + freeze new deployments. We need the runbook steps and the exact API commands. I'll draft them.

[06:05] Jordan: Quick note: we saw a weird tensor core fallback in one run, might be due to a kernel mismatch in the compile step, I tracked a grep to the build log. I'll add that to the bench notes.

[06:40] Priya: On KMS, we need to validate key rotation and HSM fallback behavior. For SOC2 audit we should have test artifacts. Evan, can we commit to a test matrix?

[07:05] Evan: Yes, Jordan and Priya to own the KMS tests. Priya will record the runbook steps and sample audit logs. Jordan will instrument a test that rotates keys during low-traffic window and validate decrypt/reencrypt behavior.

[07:40] Maya: Observability - dashboards need to show token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, and the canary vs baseline comparison. Samir, can you produce the dashboard templates?

[08:08] Samir: Yep I'll spin up dashboard templates in Grafana and share links. Will include alerts for p99 and error rate.

[08:30] Evan: Ok, about the metrics SLOs
do we have agreement on p50/p95/p99 targets? Product suggests p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 700ms for core routes.

[08:58] Jordan: Those look aggressive for the 2k sequence loads on current quantized models, p99 might be 900ms in worst-case. We can optimize kernels and batching but we should be conservative in the doc.

[09:25] Priya: Suggest p99 target 700ms for <1k seq, 900ms for 1k-2k, and a note for >2k depending on model. We'll document as conditional SLOs.

[09:55] Evan: Good, add conditional SLOs to the deck.

[10:20] Maya: I want to surface one risk: the autoscaler cooldown and the caching heuristics sometimes interact poorly during traffic ramps, causing brief 5-10s latency spikes. We've seen this in staging. We need a throttle for the cache population or smoother ramp.

[10:55] Jordan: Agreed, I have a patch that does a staggered KV prefill across nodes, reduces stampeding. I'll add the details to the bench notes.

[11:30] Priya: For deployment security, we must confirm SSO/SAML flows and service account perms, and ensure audit logs are forwarded to the central SIEM. Who owns the SIEM forwarder?

[11:58] Samir: Security infra team owns forwarding but I'll coordinate. We need to ensure log samples are in the bench artifacts.

[12:30] Evan: Ok next, timeline: target soft launch on 2026-05-27, full rollout by 2026-06-03 if all checks pass. Does that align?

[12:58] Maya: Timeline ok pending benchmarks and KMS tests. If Jordan or Priya find blockers we'll move the launch.

[13:25] Jordan: I do have one nit: can we reserve a smaller window for an emergency dry-run before soft launch? Maybe 2026-05-25 for a simulated traffic run.

[13:52] Evan: Good call. Let's schedule a simulated traffic run on 2026-05-25. Jordan will run, Maya will observe, Priya watches security, Samir watches dashboards.

[14:20] Priya: Anything on compliance docs? We should attach the SOC2 evidence to the deck. Evan we need a list of artifacts.

[14:42] Evan: I'll compile an artifacts checklist and share by 2026-05-21 with links to runbooks, test results, and logs.

[15:05] Maya: One more item — telemetry retention for launch metrics, we need 90 days retention for the first month post-launch for analysis. Is storage budget ok?

[15:35] Samir: We'll keep high-res (100ms histograms) for 30 days and aggregated for 90 days to save costs. I'll add cost estimate to the spreadsheet.

[16:00] Jordan: Confirming again I'll include both cold-start and steady-state runs, and capture the time distribution per token (embedding vs gen).

[16:25] Evan: Perfect. Let's recap owners in the deck and action items, re-share links.

[16:40] Maya: Recap: Jordan benchmarks by 5/24, sim run 5/25, Samir dashboards + runbook, Priya KMS tests by 5/26, me finalize autoscale, Evan distribute deck by 5/21.

[17:05] Evan: Great, thanks team. Any last blockers?

[17:20] (crosstalk) Jordan: none here, I'll start the bench now.

[17:35] Priya: none from security.

[17:48] Maya: ok thanks, meeting over.

[18:00] End of recording.
